entry.title: A change your toddler can hear about
entry.summary: When discussing a young toddler’s pacifier, Davies describes telling the child that a change is coming and giving extra support. The discussion is her approach, not a deadline for this age.
entry.cue: A family may be considering a change and wondering how to include the child.
detail: The book describes a gradual move toward less use and asks the adult to notice whether the child is seeking engagement, closeness, or help settling. Those possibilities are invitations to observe, not certain explanations.

Davies also describes planning the later bedtime change with the child. Her sleep chapter retains support rather than crying alone, and specialist help when persistent difficulties affect the child or family.

ageContext.bookAge: The source discusses a young toddler still using a pacifier; its first-year preference is not an 18–24 month deadline.
